title: POC: workload burn-rate, benchmarks & deployment-mode alternatives - Mariner Diagnostics
summary: AE + SE run through POC success criteria, expected workload (qps, payload sizes), burn-rate estimates, benchmark plan, and decision tradeoffs between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes. Security and data residency are constraints. Next steps include a benchmark plan, pricing estimate, and SOC2 docs share.

Schedule follow-up to review benchmark results week of 2026-12-30

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-18
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (Mariner CTO), Priya Shah (ML Eng Lead), Samir Gupta (SecOps), Jenna Park (PM)

Summary: Quick kickoff for POC scoping. Goal: decide which deployment mode makes sense (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), agree on success criteria and measurable benchmarks, and plan timeline and data/security blockers.

[00:00] Lena (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, then Marcus will run through the technical plan and we can dig into constraints.
[00:18] Alex (Mariner): Thanks Lena. Alex here, CTO. We want to make sure a pilot can show performance and cost that justify a product rollout in Q2.
[00:27] Priya (Mariner): Priya - ML lead. We'll own the sample prompts; I'll send anonymized traces. Primary model use is clinical note summarization + question-answering in downstream UI.
[00:40] Marcus (Redwood SE): Great. High-level agenda: define success metrics (latency P95, throughput qps, quality thresholds), estimate token burn-rate and cost delta across hosting modes, sketch benchmark harness and timeline.

[02:03] Marcus: Quick question on traffic shape — is traffic spiky? what concurrency do you see?
[02:10] Priya: Right now it's low volume — maybe 6 qps average, spikes to 40 qps during batch ingest windows. Payloads vary. Average prompt length 120 tokens, responses 180 tokens.
[02:28] Jenna (PM): Also need 99th percentile latency under 800ms for most UI flows, background jobs can be higher.

[03:10] Marcus: Ok that's helpful. For a POC we usually run tests at three scale points: baseline (10 qps), target (40 qps spikes), and stress (100 qps) to understand headroom and scaling.
[03:25] Alex: That stress number is more than we expect in prod, but good to validate. For regulatory reasons we may need data to stay in our EU region; can you support region pinned infra?
[03:41] Lena: Yes, we have region-aware routing for hosted, and Dedicated/Private give more control for residency. We'll cover tradeoffs shortly.

[04:50] Marcus: Let's translate Priya's numbers into burned tokens. If average in+out is ~300 tokens per request, at 40 qps that's about 12k tokens/sec, roughly 43M tokens/hour, ~1B tokens/day if sustained. For the pilot we'll likely do shorter bursts, but burn-rate matters for costing and host vs. dedicated math.
[05:18] Priya: That token calc is helpful — we won't sustain 1B tokens/day but want headroom for batch reprocessing.

[06:05] Samir (SecOps): Security constraints: SOC2 compliance required for vendor, VPC peering desired, customer-managed KMS preferable, audit logs to retain 12 months. Also we need encryption in transit and at rest.
[06:24] Lena: Redwood supports SOC2 compliant hosted offerings; for customer-managed KMS and strict network controls we recommend Dedicated or Private. Hosted can do region controls and TLS, but KMS key control is limited.

[07:10] Marcus: I'll outline technical tradeoffs now. Hosted: fastest onboarding, pay-as-you-go, Redwood handles infra and scaling; good if you prioritize time-to-value. Dedicated: reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and model pinning, with single-tenant isolation—lower latency variance and better cost predictability at committed usage. Private: full control (VPC/on-prem), customer-managed KMS, best for strict compliance, but longer lead-time and ops overhead.

[08:05] Jenna: For our board to sign off they need cost per active user and a clear runway. Can you provide burn-rate estimates for each mode?
[08:16] Lena: Yes. We'll provide a modeled estimate. Roughly, Hosted raw per-token price is highest but minimal infra overhead. Dedicated amortizes GPU cost over committed tokens — cheaper per unit at scale. Private has higher upfront infra and ops cost but gives you control and can be cheaper in very large sustained workloads.

[09:30] Marcus: On benchmarking: we want to measure P50/P95/P99 latencies, throughput at tail percentiles under realistic prompts, token-cost per request, and quality (ROUGE/F1 or a small eval set). We'll also look at cold-start behavior for KV cache and memory footprint.
[09:52] Priya: For quality we'll provide a 200-sample eval set with ground truth; we want to detect regressions >3% measured by our metric.

[11:10] Alex: How do you handle model variants if capacity is constrained? For example, fall back to a smaller quantized model?
[11:20] Marcus: We support automated fallback policies; smart routing can divert requests to a quantized variant or region with compatible model. That ties into the quality guardrails — we can set acceptable degradation thresholds.

[12:05] Samir: About telemetry — can you give us token-level cost breakdown per route and per model? We need granularity to report to finance.
[12:20] Lena: Console gives token-level and route-level cost and latency breakdowns, plus traces. For Dedicated we can expose more detailed metrics.

[13:15] Marcus: For the POC harness we'll simulate: real prompt distribution, 3 load phases (baseline/target/stress), and a set of synthetic arrivals to test burst behavior. We'll measure tail latencies at target spikes and model the cost.

[14:30] Priya: How long do you need to run these tests to be meaningful?
[14:36] Marcus: For throughput and warm-cache behavior, a sustained 48-hour run is ideal — it shows steady-state behavior, autoscaling, and cache effectiveness. For quick validation we can do a 2-hour spike test first.

[15:20] Alex: Timeline concerns — we want vendor selection by mid-Jan to budget for Q2 rollout. Can you hit that?
[15:28] Lena: Yes. Proposed timeline: benchmark plan and data exchange this week, Redwood runs tests and shares results by 12/29, follow-up week of 12/30 to decide hosting mode for a 6-week pilot starting early Jan.

[16:10] Jenna: What are the gating success criteria for the POC?
[16:17] Marcus: We recommend three gates: (1) performance gate — P95 < 800ms under target spike and error rate <0.1%; (2) cost gate — modeled cost per 1k active users within 15% of finance target; (3) quality gate — no more than 3% regression on eval metrics.

[17:05] Priya: For the quality gate can we have automatic regression alerts?
[17:10] Marcus: Yes, Redwood Optimize supports quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. We'll wire those up for the eval set.

[18:02] Samir: Network architecture — if we go Dedicated but still want KMS control, is that supported?
[18:10] Lena: Dedicated can integrate with customer KMS in many cases; Private gives most control. We'll need Samir's KMS provider details to validate.

[19:00] Alex: Is benchmarking in Hosted sandbox representative of Dedicated latency?
[19:07] Marcus: Hosted sandbox will be slightly different — Dedicated reduces multi-tenant noise and lets you pin model versions. We'll supply a host vs. dedicated delta estimate from prior benchmarks, but for final numbers we recommend a short Dedicated run if you commit.

[20:15] Priya: Can we do sample runs with our exact model weights or only curated models?
[20:22] Marcus: For Hosted we provide Redwood-curated models; Dedicated/Private allow custom model onboarding. If you need exact weights onboarded, Dedicated is the usual path — onboarding takes a few days to validate.

[21:05] Jenna: Cost modeling — do you provide amortized GPU cost at various commit levels?
[21:12] Lena: Yes, we'll share a pricing template showing per-token, per-hour GPU amortization, and recommended commit tiers.

[22:00] Marcus: A note on caching: automatic prefix/KV caching can cut token cost and latency for repeated context. For summarization flows with repeated patient history fragments, caching helps a lot. We'll measure cache hit rate during the 48-hour run.

[23:05] Priya: Good point — we have repeated blocks. We'll annotate traces where caching looks likely.

[24:22] Alex: Any compliance red flags for Private option if we go on-prem? Ops overhead concern is real.
[24:30] Lena: Private will require infra setup and operational handoff; Redwood offers a private control plane and an optional on-prem package but expect multi-week setup. For time-to-value, Dedicated strikes a middle ground.

[25:50] Samir: Audit log retention — can retention be configured to 12+ months? Also, are logs exportable to our SIEM?
[25:58] Marcus: Yes, audit logs are configurable; Dedicated and Private offer more retention options and direct S3/Kafka export hooks for your SIEM.

[27:12] Jenna: Are there any known performance regressions with quantized variants for summarization tasks?
[27:20] Marcus: Some quantization approaches affect generation quality on open-ended summarization; we'll include quantized and float baselines in the quality checks. If degradation exceeds your threshold we'll avoid fallback.

[28:35] Priya: Can you show us a sample benchmark report format?
[28:40] Marcus: Yes, we'll attach an example — it'll have latency histograms, throughput over time, cache-hit curves, cost breakdown, and a small quality evaluation table.

[30:00] Alex: About the decision criteria between modes — can you summarize recommended triggers that would push us to Dedicated vs Private?
[30:08] Lena: Yes: choose Hosted if you need fastest time-to-value and volume is modest; Dedicated if you expect predictable sustained throughput with cost predictability or need single-tenant isolation; Private if you require customer-managed KMS, strict network isolation, or air-gapped deployment. Typical trigger: committing to sustained monthly tokens above the Dedicated break-even threshold or strict regulatory/legal controls needing Private.

[31:25] Priya: Break-even threshold ballpark?
[31:30] Lena: We'll model it, but historically we've seen Dedicated become economical when sustained token consumption is in the mid-to-high hundreds of millions per month depending on model size and commit. We'll provide a concrete table in the pricing template.

[33:00] Marcus: On runbook and rollouts: we recommend canarying new model versions, automatic fallback to previous variant on regressions, and health checks tied to response quality.

[34:12] Jenna: For pilot acceptance — who signs off on the quality gate? Priya and Alex?
[34:18] Alex: Priya signs off on quality, I'll sign off on infra and cost. Jenna will own product acceptance.

[35:05] Samir: We need a short security review before any Dedicated or Private provisioning. Lena, can you share the security pack?
[35:12] Lena: Yes — I'll send SOC2 report, pen-test summary, and network architecture note. Expect that in an email after this call.

[36:00] Priya: Any special notes about model warm-up and KV cache priming for the test harness?
[36:07] Marcus: We'll prime KV caches with representative contexts and run a warm-up period before measuring steady-state. We'll include both cold and warm metrics.

[37:40] Alex: How long does onboarding a custom model to Dedicated take?
[37:46] Marcus: Typically 2-5 business days to validate weights and run sample inferences; longer if quantized kernels need extra tuning. We'll factor that into the timeline.

[39:05] Jenna: For reporting to finance, can you give an expected cost range (low/med/high) per 1000 active users for each hosting mode?
[39:15] Lena: We'll produce a matrix with conservative, expected, and optimistic scenarios. It'll include token price, infra amortization, and support fees.

[40:40] Priya: Any obstacles you see for a quick POC that would delay into Jan?
[40:45] Marcus: Main blockers are: (1) secure transfer of traces (anonymization), (2) KMS validation if you want customer keys for Dedicated, and (3) any legal procurement lead time. Technical work is small and we'd run in hosted sandbox initially.

[41:30] Samir: On anonymization — we'll strip PII and ship example traces. Samir will coordinate.

[42:10] Lena: Recap of immediate deliverables: Marcus will publish the benchmark harness and schedule; Priya will send traces; Lena sends security docs and pricing template.

[43:00] Marcus: Proposed short-run plan: 2-hour spike test this week to validate harness, then a 48-hour sustained run in hosted sandbox. We'll capture latency, throughput, token burn, and cache hit rate.

[44:20] Alex: If the 48-hour run looks good, what's the next step?
[44:25] Lena: We'll present results and recommend either staying Hosted for pilot or provisioning Dedicated for the 6-week pilot. If Dedicated is selected, there's a short provisioning and onboarding window.

[45:40] Jenna: Anything else about legal / procurement we should know?
[45:46] Samir: We'll loop legal but expect standard enterprise SLA review if we move to Dedicated.

[46:30] Marcus: A few technical clarifications captured: measure cold vs warm KV latency, track model fallback rates, collect memory/GPU utilization, and measure autoscaler behavior under the target spike.

[47:55] Priya: Sounds good. We'll prioritize the traces export.

[49:10] Lena: Thanks everyone. I'll send notes and next steps. Marcus will follow up with the benchmark harness link.

[50:02] Alex: Appreciate the clear gates. Talk soon.
[50:10] Jenna: Thanks all.
[51:00] [meeting ends]
